boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Prairie D'Ane (Moscow) record (April 9-13, 1864) in the Camden Expedition [April 1864]. The frozen record also carries the names Gum Grove and Moscow; the April 10-12 fighting on the prairie and the April 13 rear-guard action at Moscow fall within its interval and are recorded as one record without adding their figures. The march on to Camden (April 14-15) is context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, foraging and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Department of Arkansas [US] and District of Arkansas [CS]; the live field reads zero. Price says Thayer's command joined Steele with 5,500 men and ten guns, that Gano's brigade of 500 and Tandy Walker's brigade of about 1,000 reinforced him, and that Thayer's rear guard at Moscow was some 3,000 with ten guns. Britton says Thayer's division was about five thousand with twelve field guns and two howitzers.
claims.rationale: Interested and retrospective estimates of components on different days; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Price says he withdrew from the prairie by design, and that at Moscow Dockery took and lost a section of artillery before the enemy retreated in the night. Britton says Price abandoned his works without resistance and the Moscow attackers were driven from the field and pursued about three miles.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The march into Camden is campaign context.

claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The live figures have no inspected basis.

open_questions: Steele's reports (No. 2), Salomon's, Engelmann's, Garrett's and the Frontier Division itinerary (Nos. 5, 19, 21, 23), Thayer's report (not listed in this volume's Camden reports), Marmaduke's and Shelby's reports (Nos. 71, 73) and Maxey's report remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam's, 1899) is a retrospective history described on its title page as based upon official reports and the author's observations; it gives figures from Union and Confederate reports and incomplete Confederate returns, so it is not independent of the Official Records families. Price's report dated Camden, May 1864 is one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
